prerequisites: A B1 English level is generally required to adequately access the course, as the objective is to reach the officially required B2 technical level. Students starting without this level in oral and written communication and comprehension will have serious problems passing the subject.

learning_outcomes.text: Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society.
Demonstrate an entrepreneurial attitude in the design, development and execution of solutions that represent a novelty or advance in the field of the discipline.
Function effectively in a team whose members together provide leadership and create a collaborative and inclusive environment in the organization and coordination of work.
Collaborate proactively in the development of work, setting goals and meeting objectives.
Structure discourse to favor the understanding of the objectives, actions and/or results of one's own work.
Develop professional texts or scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the discipline.
Adapt the organization of content and the use of verbal and non-verbal language to argue in various situations and/or before various audiences.

teaching_methods: Individual and group preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects

assessment_methods.method: Final Written Exam - Questions related to book topics

assessment_rules: In the first convocation, the final grade is split 50% continuous assessment (integrated project, oral presentation, review tests) and 50% final written exam, but continuous assessment grades are only counted if a minimum of 2 out of 5 is obtained in the final exam. An alternative scheme applies for students exempt from the integrated project, where continuous assessment is 20% and the final exam (written and oral) is 80%, with the continuous assessment grade considered only if a minimum of 3.2 out of 8 is obtained in the final exam and a minimum of 2.4/6 in the written part to take the oral. For the second convocation, students can choose between three different grading paths, including a 100% final exam option (70% written, 30% oral) and options combining continuous assessment, all subject to specific minimum scores. The use of AI tools is strictly regulated, with different levels of permission and citation requirements, and non-compliance is considered academic fraud.
